scope: Cosmos native DROID multiview dataset iterations v1 through v5
summary: Five immutable dataset attempts exposed Git-metadata, missing-caption, exact-window, short-episode, and temporal-resampling defects before formal training; none of these superseded datasets is accepted for model fitting.
evidence: Composite v1 stopped because Git provenance was hard-coded incorrectly; v2 stopped on empty prompts.
Composite v3 proved the 33-frame layout only, while upstream training requires a 93-frame window and fails when source length is exactly 93.
Source v3 rejected reserved episode 21 as too short for that attempted contract; v4 correctly produced 93 native-layout composites with 86 train, 2 validation, and 3 final samples.
Pre-training audit then found that v4 first sampled source at 8 FPS and subsequently repeated frames to 16 FPS, so v4 was rejected despite its valid geometry and split contract.
The v5 direct-16-FPS rebuild was intentionally stopped after 50 camera clips when the stronger two-window-per-training-episode v6 contract was chosen; its partial directory is preserved.
lessons: Dataset acceptance must cover temporal sampling as well as dimensions, hashes, captions, and split leakage.
Matching the model's 16 FPS training distribution at source extraction avoids systematic adjacent-frame pairs introduced by an 8-to-16 FPS second stage.
limitations: These attempts establish engineering failures and corrections only; no model-quality milestone follows from them.
The 15 FPS source still requires a single nearest-time sampling step to the model's 16 FPS contract.
next_actions: Accept only the two-window native-16-FPS v6 source and a newly built composite after all probes and leakage checks pass.
